{{Quote|Oh, my bones are aching. Storm's coming up, Ani. You better get home quick!|Jira|<ref name="TPM" />}}
'''Jira''' was an impoverished merchant who ran a [[Jira's fruit stand|fruit stand]] in the [[City/Legends|city]] [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] for many [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. She sold various [[Fruit/Legends|fruits]], [[Vegetable/Legends|vegetables]], and other wares, becoming a permanent fixture of Mos Espa's streets, although she lived in extreme poverty. In her old age, Jira was friends with the [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] child [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], with whom she would occasionally share free produce in exchange for repairs on her equipment.

In [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]], Jira helped Skywalker and his friends [[Kitster Chanchani Banai]], [[Pala Kwi'teksa]], and [[Dorn (Bothan)|Dorn]] coordinate the [[Rescue of the Ghostlings|rescue]] of several [[Ghostling]] children who had been kidnapped on behalf of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder/Legends|Gardulla Besadii the Elder]]. The vendor offered her [[Jira's apartment|apartment]] as a meeting place, provided practical advice to help the children in their plot, and collected financial donations from enslaved people in Mos Espa to help [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggle]] the Ghostlings offworld. When the plan nearly went awry, Jira attempted to persuade Skywalker to take the opportunity to leave Tatooine, but the boy chose to stay and saw to the successful escape of the Ghostlings with Jira's help.

[[32 BBY/Legends|The following year]], Jira's cooling unit broke down, and Skywalker found a replacement for her in [[Wald's Parts|Watto's junkyard]]. He told Jira about it shortly afterwards when he purchased fruit from her for his new offworld acquaintances, [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], and [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]]. The interaction was interrupted when Jira alerted the boy to an oncoming [[Sandstorm/Legends|sandstorm]]. Skywalker soon after secured his freedom by winning the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Podracing/Legends|podrace]] and stopped by Jira's stall on his way off Tatooine to give her [[Currency/Legends|money]] to buy a new cooling unit. The two friends never saw each other again, and Jira was nowhere to be found in Mos Espa when Skywalker returned there [[22 BBY/Legends|ten years later]].

==Biography==
===Mos Espa vendor===
{{Quote|Fruit. Get your fruit here.|Jira's sales pitch|<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8">''[[Episode I Adventures 8: Trouble on Tatooine]]''</ref>}}
Jira was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] from<ref name="DB" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Desert/Legends|desert]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="TPM" /> [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="DB" /> Jira preferred to keep the explanation of how she ended up on Tatooine to herself, with some speculating that she had once been [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] and gained freedom. Through hard work over many [[Standard year/Legends|years]], Jira acquired a [[Jira's fruit stand|fruit stand]] and continued to work hard to maintain it and earn a living. She became a permanent fixture in the [[City/Legends|city]] [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]], an unusual feat given the constant movement of people through it. Jira's wares included [[Fruit/Legends|fruits]] such as [[Pallie/Legends|pallies]] and [[pika]], [[Vegetable/Legends|vegetables]],<ref name="Fact File 133">{{FactFile|133|JIR 1-2|Jira}}</ref> drinks,<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6">''[[Episode I Adventures 6: The Hunt for Anakin Skywalker]]''</ref> and other popular crops.<ref name="Fact File 133" />

[[File:Nobot.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Jira would share the story of Nobot (pictured) for a price.]]
Jira was known to share the story of the mysterious wandering [[3PO-series protocol droid/Legends|3PO-series protocol droid]] [[Nobot/Legends|Nobot]] for the price of two [[Peggat/Legends|peggats]]. According to her, the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] appeared in Mos Espa [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] prior<ref name="Nobot">{{DB|droid|nobot|Nobot}}</ref> to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places the events of {{Film|I}} in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].</ref> and was the only survivor of the [[Death/Legends|murder]] of a young [[Unidentified pregnant woman|pregnant woman]]. The droid's communication module echoed the woman's cries for help and her final shrill scream followed by a long period of silence, interupted by static noises until the recording repeated itself. Some believed that Nobot was the murderer in Jira's tale. Other stall owners who worked near Jira began telling their own versions of Nobot's story with more fanciful anecdotes and unusual occurences, although Jira was regarded as the superior storyteller.<ref name="Nobot" />

By the [[Time/Legends|time]] Jira was an older woman, she had befriended the [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] Human boy [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]],<ref name="Fact File 133" /> who had arrived on Tatooine in [[38 BBY/Legends|38 BBY]].<ref name="Jedi vs Sith">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']] states that [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] was born in [[41 BBY/Legends|41 BBY]] and was believed to have just turned three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] old when he arrived on Tatooine, therefore, his arrival on Tatooine took place in [[38 BBY/Legends|38 BBY]].</ref> The two had a useful relationship: Skywalker helped resolve issues with Jira's [[Cooling unit/Legends|cooling unit]] through repairs and sourcing of spare parts free of charge, and Jira occasionally provided the boy with free fruit.<ref name="Fact File 133" />

===Rescuing the Ghostling children===
====Meeting with the conspirators====
{{Quote|Why don't you children come out of the sun? It's much cooler in my apartment.|Jira discretely arranges for the children to discuss the matter of the Ghostlings with her|<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" />}}
[[File:Jira.png|thumb|left|250px|Jira at her fruit stall.]]
In [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]],<ref name="Episode I Adventures date">''[[Episode I Adventures 6: The Hunt for Anakin Skywalker]]'' states that its events occur a [[Standard week/Legends|week]] before the [[Standard year/Legends|annual]] [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]]. ''[[Episode I Adventures 5: The Ghostling Children]]'' takes place in the preceeding [[Standard year/Legends|days]], and describes [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], who was born in [[41 BBY/Legends|41 BBY]] according to [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']], as older than the eight-year-old [[Arawynne]]. Skywalker is also depicted competing in the [[Podracing/Legends|podrace]] and crashing at the conclusion of ''[[Episode I Adventures 8: Trouble on Tatooine]]'', prior to his winning of the [[Boonta Eve Classic (32 BBY)/Legends|race]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] as depicted in {{Film|I}} and dated by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. Therefore, the events of ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Adventures]]'' 5&ndash;8 must take place in [[33 BBY/Legends|33 BBY]].</ref> on an occasion where Skywalker was ordered by his enslaver, [[Watto/Legends|Watto]], to purchase materials from [[Jawa/Legends|Jawas]],<ref name="Episode I Adventures 5">''[[Episode I Adventures 5: The Ghostling Children]]''</ref> a species of scavengers,<ref name="CSWE Jawa">{{CSWECite|II|143|Jawa}}</ref> in the [[Jundland Wastes/Legends|Jundland Wastes]], the child's throat became parched, and he found himself wishing that he had stopped by Jira's stall for a cool drink earlier.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 5" />

Shortly afterward, a week before the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Podracing/Legends|podrace]], Skywalker met with his friends, the Human [[Kitster Chanchani Banai]], the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Pala Kwi'teksa]], and the [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] [[Dorn (Bothan)|Dorn]], at Jira's stall. The [[Standard day/Legends|night]] prior, the children had [[Rescue of the Ghostlings|rescued]] a group of captive [[Ghostling]] children&mdash;including [[Alamar]], [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Arawynne]], [[Borofir]], [[Coniel]],<ref name="Episode I Adventures 5" /> and [[Conno]]<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8" />&mdash;from the [[Gardulla's palace|palace]] of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Gardulla Besadii the Elder/Legends|Gardulla Besadii the Elder]], and had learned that the Hutts were likely to find the culprits after analysing a sample of Kwi'teksa's skin that had been left behind. During the meeting, Jira locked up her stall, placed a [[Color/Legends|green-colored]] drink on the table in front of Skywalker, and invited the children to her [[Jira's apartment|apartment]]. Skywalker attempted to refuse her invitation to avoid involving her, but the old vendor revealed that she was aware that Gardulla had posted a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] for four children. At her apartment, Jira had to shoo two Jawas away that were peaking through her door before entering. The bare state of her apartment embarrassed Skywalker, who thought of the many times he had received free drinks from the vendor.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" />

====Planning the operation====
{{Quote|There is always hope. Most slaves have a ''little'' money. All together, maybe it will be enough.|Jira, supporting Skywalker and his friends in smuggling the Ghostlings off Tatooine.|<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" />}}
[[File:Ghostling_child.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Jira became involved in the plot to help the Ghostling children (one pictured) escape Tatooine.]]
Jira directed the four children to sit down and questioned what they had been thinking in liberating the Ghostlings. Skywalker explained that they were trying to save their lives, for which Jira praised the boy's kindness. She then challenged them to consider how they would protect themselves in the aftermath and how they planned to help the Ghostlings return to their home on the planet [[Datar/Legends|Datar]]. Dorn suggested that they would be able to send them on a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] heading in Datar's direction.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" />

Jira revealed that she knew of a tertiary contact who could smuggle the Ghostlings off Tatooine for a high price, which none of the present company would be able to afford, especially given the limited window of time until the Hutts located Kwi'teksa due to her [[Slave tracking device|transmitter]]. The old woman refuted Banai's suggestion that Kwi'teksa hide underground, knowing that the Twi'lek's enslavers would think to check Mos Espa's sewers and tunnels first. This prompted Skywalker to suggest that he could build a [[Jammer/Legends|signal jammer]] to hide Kwi'teksa's location.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" />

Dorn then questioned how they would be able to secure enough money for the operation, to which Jira responded that they needed to have hope and that many enslaved individuals had a small amount of currency which could be pooled together. The vendor instructed Kwi'teksa to hide and for the other children to leave her apartment one by one and then to return at nighttime, when she would update them on any developments. Jira was able to use her connections to learn that a ship that could [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggle]] the Ghostlings offworld,<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" /> captained by [[Rakir Banai]]&mdash;who was coincidentally Kitster's [[Parent/Legends|father]]<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8" />&mdash;would land the following night.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" />

====Further obstacles====
{{Quote|A friend has made some contacts, and a ship will touch down tomorrow night. But we must have the money for the Ghostling children by then.|Jira, explaining the situation to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" />}}
[[File:Jira_detail.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Jira]]
Jira, Kitster, and Dorn returned to her apartment at night, followed later by Skywalker. The woman detailed when the ship would arrive and that, for the rescue to succeed, they would need to keep Kwi'teksa hidden and source enough currency to pay the smugglers. The children then explained the steps they had taken to successfully hide the Twi'lek from the Hutts, and Jira instructed them to speak no further and reminded them that they still had work to do. The children shared the money they had saved up, although Jira encouraged them to continue to acquire more before they left her apartment.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" />

The following day, Dorn, who was being intimidated by the Hutt [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] into giving up Kwi'teksa's location, waited by Jira's stall. Skywalker dropped off a signal jammer to his Bothan friend to help protect him.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 7">''[[Episode I Adventures 7: Capture Arawynne]]''</ref> Jira continued attempting to secure the necessary funds from the donations of enslaved people, but was unable to get enough. When was selling fruit later that day, Skywalker dropped by her stall and informed her, to Jira's dejection, that his three friends and the Ghostling children had been captured and slated for execution. Jira discretely pretended that she was selling Skywalker an item at her apartment while packing up her stall.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8" />

====Money problems====
{{Quote|I didn't get the money. I got part of it, but not nearly enough. Maybe if we give them the money I've got, the smugglers will take you away, instead.|Jira, to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8" />}}
[[File:Tatooine_TPM.png|thumb|right|250px|Jira raised funds to help smuggle the Ghostlings off Tatooine.]]
At the apartment, Jira told Skywalker that his friends were likely to pay for their kindness with their lives, and pleaded with him to take the [[Transport/Legends|transport]] meant for the Ghostlings, which was due to land in less than four [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] time at sunset. Skywalker was indignant and reminded Jira of her hopeful encouragement earlier, to which the woman sadly explained that she had not secured enough money, although she hoped that the smugglers would accept the funds she had raised to secure Skywalker's safety. The boy told her to find more money and that he would be ready at sunset, along with his friends.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8" />

Although she was unable to secure enough money, Jira later headed out of Mos Espa to [[Bantha Rock]], with the plan being for her to signal to the smugglers when Skywalker had arrived. Skywalker eventually reached her location in a [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] along with those he had been able to rescue, which included Kwi'teksa, Banai, and most of the Ghostling children. Dorn and Conno had been initially unable to escape. The plan was for all of the children, including the Tatooinians, to board the ship to safety. Jira explained that she had still not found enough currency, but Skywalker revealed that he had stolen a stash of coins from a dozen worlds from [[Morseerian/Legends|Morseerian]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] during the rescue and gave them to the old woman.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8" />

====Successful rescue====
{{Quote|Anakin, Kitster, we have a few coins left over. I want you to have them.''"<br />"''Us? But that money belongs to the slaves.''"<br />"''They gave the money to you children, to help you buy your freedom. I think you should keep it, and spend it wisely.|Jira, giving the leftover money to Anakin Skywalker and Kitster Banai|<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8" />}}
[[File:RakirBanai.png|thumb|left|200px|Jira arranged for Rakir Banai (pictured) to smuggle the Ghostlings off Tatooine.]]
Jira stood on a rock and used a [[Glowrod/Legends|glowrod]] to signal to the smugglers in a coded movement, after which Rakir landed his [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]]. Jira handed her bag of coins to him, and the smuggler confirmed that it would be enough for him to tightly fit all of the children aboard his ship, although Skywalker chose to stay behind. Relieved that their scheme was working, Jira tearfully said goodbye to Kwi'teksa and the Ghostlings. She also hugged Kitster, tussled his [[Hair/Legends|hair]], and expressed gladness at his newfound freedom while acknowledging that she would miss him. Kitster reciprocated her feelings, after which he recognized that Rakir was his long-lost father, although he did not reveal it to anyone.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8" />

Dorn and Conno then arrived in a landspeeder stolen from Jabba, and Jira and Skywalker rushed over and led them to the ship. When Rakir explained that he would not be able to take all of the children, Jira offered more of the money Skywalker had given her, but the smuggler explained that the issue was that his ship's life support systems would be unable to support all of them. This led Kitster to decide to stay on Tatooine without revealing his recognition of his father, as he believed he had a better chance of remaining anonymous than Dorn or Kwi'teksa for his role in the recent operation.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8" />

Once the ship departed Tatooine, Jira, Skywalker, and Kitster watched from a distance as the [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]], who had been hunting the Ghostlings and witnessed the ship's departure, furiously fired a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] into the stolen landspeeder. The trio laughed and cheered before returning to Mos Espa on the vehicle. En route, Jira offered the remaining funds, which totaled one thousand units of currency, to the two boys, encouraging them to spend it wisely. Skywalker dropped the old woman off at her apartment before dropping Kitster off and returning home.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8" />

===Events of 32 BBY===
====Broken equipment====
{{Quote|Don't worry, I'll find what I'm looking for! I always do!''"<br />"''Perhaps, Anakin Skywalker. You're a special boy.|Anakin Skywalker promises to find a cooling unit for Jira|<ref name="Episode I: Anakin Skywalker">''[[Episode I: Anakin Skywalker]]''</ref>}}
In approximately 32 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]],<ref name="Pit Droid Date">''[[Catch That Pit Droid!]]'' ends during the events of {{Film|I}}, which occurred in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> a malfunctioning [[DUM-series pit droid/Legends|DUM-series pit droid]] ran from Watto's shop and crashed into Jira's fruit stand while being pursued by Skywalker and Watto. The child apologised to Jira as the two continued their chase.<ref name="Catch that Pit Droid">''[[Catch That Pit Droid!]]''</ref>

[[File:Anakin_and_Jira.png|thumb|right|250px|Jira had a productive friendship with the young Anakin Skywalker.]]
Later that week, the power couplings fused within the cooling unit Jira used to store her fruit, rendering it inoperable and distressing the woman as she was unable to afford a new device. As she sat at her stall, Jira was approached by Anakin, whose mother, [[Shmi Skywalker Lars/Legends|Shmi Skywalker]], had tasked her son with purchasing fruit from Jira's stall. Anakin, along with his friends Banai and [[W. Wald]], observed that something was wrong, and Jira explained her plight before providing Anakin with pika fruit she had set aside for the Skywalkers. Anakin promised to look for a replacement cooling unit in Watto's junkyard. Jira doubted that the boy would find the replacement she needed, but Anakin insisted that he would as he walked away, prompting Jira to acknowledge that he could succeed. Anakin was indeed successful in finding another cooling unit and was excited to repair it and pass it on to Jira.<ref name="Episode I: Anakin Skywalker" />

====Skywalker's last goodbye====
{{Quote|Oh, I’ll miss you, Ani. You’re the kindest boy in the galaxy. You take care.|Jira's farewell to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="TPM novel">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref>}}
Before he could arrange to give Jira the cooling unit, Skywalker encountered a group of offworlders hoping to purchase a [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] from Watto, which included [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], the disguised [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen of Naboo]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], and the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]].<ref name="Episode I: Anakin Skywalker" /> Skywalker befriended the group and, with the intention of spending more time with Amidala, later persuaded them to join him on a short trip to Jira's stand. There, Skywalker greeted the vendor with a hug and exuberantly told her about the cooling unit he had found, promising to fix it up for her. The vendor brushed Skywalker's cheek and praised him for his efforts.<ref name="TPM novel" />

Skywalker then ordered four pallies from Jira, but changed his order to three when he realized that he only had three [[Trugut/Legends|truguts]] to spare, using the excuse that he was no longer hungry. Once the exchange had been made,<ref name="TPM novel" /> Jira's bones began to ache, alerting her to an oncoming sandstorm. She informed Skywalker,<ref name="TPM" /> after which a sharp gust of wind sent debris flying.<ref name="TPM novel" /> Skywalker and his new friends left as Jira began packing up her stall,<ref name="TPM" /> with the boy shouting goodbye to her amongst the winds.<ref name="TPM novel" />

[[File:Farewell_to_Jira.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Anakin Skywalker says farewell to Jira.]]
Shortly thereafter, Skywalker won that year's [[Boonta Eve Classic (32 BBY)/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] and was liberated from slavery due to a [[Gambling/Legends|wager]] placed by Jinn. On his way to leave the planet with the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], the boy insisted that they stop by Jira's stand, where he gave the vendor a handful of credits from selling his [[Anakin Skywalker's Podracer/Legends|podracer]]. He told her to buy a new cooling unit to soothe his concerns for her. Jira was astonished and asked Skywalker for a hug, which he reciprocated. She called him the kindest boy in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]],<ref name="TPM novel" /> wagged a finger at him, and urged him to take care.<ref name="Rise">''[[The Rise and Fall of Darth Vader]]''</ref> A [[DRK-1 Dark Eye probe droid/Legends|DRK-1 Dark Eye probe droid]] seeking out Skywalker and Jinn for the [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] then flew past Jira's stand.<ref name="Farewell to Jira">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''&mdash;[[Content cut from Star Wars#Episode_I_The_Phantom_Menace|Deleted Scene: Farewell to Jira]]</ref> Days later, Skywalker wrote about his interactions with Jira in his [[Anakin Skywalker's journal|journal]] shortly after the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]].<ref name="Journal" /> The two friends never saw each other again, and Jira was nowhere to be found in Mos Espa when Skywalker returned there as a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] ten years later.<ref name="Fact File 95">{{FactFile2014|95|JIR 1-2|Jira}}</ref> in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].<ref name="NEC AOTC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places the events of {{Film|II}} in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]].</ref>

==Personality and traits==
===Tatooine survivor and appearance===
{{Quote|Bend like a pika bush in a sandstorm.|Jira's personal philosophy|<ref name="Fact File 133" />}}
[[File:Mos_Espa_2.png|thumb|right|350px|Jira survived in poverty on the streets of Mos Espa for years.]]
Jira was a kind<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" /> and jolly woman,<ref name="DB" /> and a wise observer of the wide range of criminals that passed through Mos Espa. To some, she appeared old, bent, weak, and feeble, but in reality, Jira had the strength and toughness necessary to survive the rough streets of Mos Espa. Through consistent hard work, she was able to maintain her fruit stall and became the equivalent of a landmark in the city. Jira had the knowledge necessary to ensure that her products lasted as long as possible so that they remained edible by the time they reached her customers. Her years of experience on Tatooine had taught her that flexibility was essential for survival, a philosophy she applied in the portable design of her fruit stand. Due to the limited availability of [[Water/Legends|water]] on Tatooine, Jira refused to share her methods for growing her produce, knowing that it would cost her livelihood if anyone else were able to replicate it.<ref name="Fact File 133" /> 

Jira was extremely poor and had few possessions, although from Anakin Skywalker's perspective, it seemed not to bother her. She did not lock her apartment, either due to having her possessions already stolen or believing that she had nothing of value worth stealing. She charged little more for drinks at her stall than what they cost to make, and Skywalker wondered whether her poverty stemmed from donating money to noble causes.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" /> The aged vendor knew all of the best spots in town to place her mobile fruit stand, which helped when she saw trouble brewing or needed to evacuate due to an incoming [[Sandstorm/Legends|sandstorm]]. Other residents of Mos Espa knew that, if Jira began packing her things, that they would be wise to do the same.<ref name="Fact File 133" />

A Human woman, Jira had gray braided hair that descended past her shoulders, green [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], and tanned skin.<ref name="DB" /> She found Tatooine's heat difficult to cope with.<ref name="Journal">''[[Star Wars Journal: Anakin Skywalker]]''</ref>

===Relationship with Anakin Skywalker===
{{Quote|Ghostlings are very frail. It was kind of you to try to help. But now, how are you going to save yourselves?|Jira raises practical concerns to Skywalker and his friends during the rescue of the Ghostlings|<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" />}}
[[File:AnakinSkywalker-TPMpromo.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Jira had a productive friendship with Anakin Skywalker (pictured).]]
Jira had a close,<ref name="Encyclopedia">{{CSWECite|II|166|Jira}}</ref> reciprocal relationship with the young Anakin Skywalker. She occasionally provided him with a free piece of fruit in exchange for equipment repairs,<ref name="Fact File 133" /> alongside free drinks.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" /> She regarded Skywalker as a special boy and expressed gratitude for his support of her. In turn, Skywalker showed concern for Jira's wellbeing when trying to locate a replacement cooling unit for her,<ref name="Episode I: Anakin Skywalker" /> to the extent that he gave her money to purchase a new one after winning it in the Boonta Eve Classic.<ref name="TPM novel" />

While helping to secure the safety of the Ghostling children, Jira provided pragmatic advice to help Skywalker and his friends, praising their kindness while directing them to plan their next steps and ensure their own safety. She initially encouraged them that there was always hope<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" /> while later reminding them of the dangers involved in risking their lives for others.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8" /> She offered her apartment as a space for the children to discuss their plans safely, aware that Mos Espa contained potential [[Spy/Legends|spies]].<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" /> Jira also was able to reach out to the enslaved population of Mos Espa to collect donations to help smuggle them offworld, and used her connections to secure the passage required for them. When Skywalker's friends were captured, she attempted to save the boy by encouraging him to take the transport meant for the Ghostlings for himself. After the Ghostlings had been successfully taken from Tatooine, Jira insisted on giving the leftover money that she had raised for them to Skywalker and Banai.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8" />

==Skills and abilities==
Jira was able to identify changes in Tatooine's weather based on various aches and pains in her bones.<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> She had the skills and knowledge necessary to grow food in Tatooine's difficult desert conditions, to the point that she could maintain a steady supply all [[Standard year/Legends|year]] round.<ref name="Fact File 133" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|My cooling unit broke down, Annie ''[sic]''. The power couplings fused. I can't afford a new one.|Jira, to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="Episode I: Anakin Skywalker" />}}
[[File:Jira_fruit_stand.png|thumb|right|250px|Jira's fruit stand.]]
Jira used a makeshift<ref name="TPM novel" /> mobile fruit stall to earn a living, which included a shade canopy<ref name="Fact File 133" /> held up by bent poles<ref name="TPM novel" /> that lacked enough shade for her to stand in.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 8" /> It could be packed up quickly for relocation along Mos Espa's streets when necessary.<ref name="Fact File 133" /> When her shop was set up, Jira arranged her wares in boxes on a rack tilted towards the streets.<ref name="TPM novel" /> She relied on a cooling unit to keep her wares fresh, though this was normally an outdated and bulky model that she had rescued from a trash pile. She also carried a fruit [[Knife/Legends|knife]] and rode an [[Eopie/Legends|eopie]],<ref name="Fact File 133" /> a quadruped pack [[Mammal/Legends|mammal]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> Every day, the woman wore the same<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" /> simple clothes that were patched and well-worn,<ref name="TPM novel" /> but always clean.<ref name="Journal" /> She lived in an apartment in a narrow alley in Mos Espa with very few possessions, which included a [[Sleeper (furniture)|bed]], a ragged pillow, two shelves, and a couple machines. Her residence was missing features typical of Tatooine settlements, such as a moisture seal or electronics in the [[Pourstone/Legends|pourstone]] walls.<ref name="Episode I Adventures 6" />

==Behind the scenes==
===''The Phantom Menace''===
[[File:MargaretTowner.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Jira was played by Margaret Towner in ''The Phantom Menace''.]]
Jira was created<ref name="DB" /> by ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]]<ref name="Illustrated Screenplay">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace Illustrated Screenplay|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace Illustrated Screenplay'']]</ref> in the revised rough draft of the [[prequel trilogy]] film {{Film|I}}.<ref name="DB" /> The scene where Jira sells fruit to Anakin Skywalker went through very few changes in subsequent drafts of the script.<ref name="Insider's Guide">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref> Jira was played by actress [[Margaret Towner]],<ref name="TPM" /> who was cast in [[1997]] after receiving an invitation to interview for the role with Lucas at [[Wikipedia:Bray Film Studios|Bray Film Studios]], although she had never heard of the writer-director prior to their meeting.<ref name="Obituary">{{WebCite|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/obituaries/2017/05/04/margaret-towner-veteran-actress-appeared-star-wars-franchise|text=Margaret Towner, veteran actress who appeared in Star Wars franchise &ndash; obituary|date=2017-05-04|work=[[Wikipedia:The Daily Telegraph|''The Daily Telegraph'']]|archivedate=20241119063624}}</ref> Filming for scenes set in the exteriors of Mos Espa took place in the [[Wikipedia:Sahara|Sahara Desert]] in [[Tunisia]] over two weeks beginning on [[July 28]], 1997.<ref name="Insider's Guide" />

During the film's editing process, the dialogue between Skywalker and Jira in the aforementioned scene was shortened considerably.<ref name="Insider's Guide" /> Additionally, the scene where Skywalker says goodbye to Jira was filmed but ultimately cut from the finished film,<ref name="Farewell to Jira" /> which premiered on [[May 19]], [[1999]].<ref name="Year by Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref> Jira first publicly appeared in ''Star Wars'' media<ref name="TPM novel" /> on [[April 21]], 1999,<ref name="Year by Year" /> when the film's [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]] by [[Terry Brooks]] was published.<ref name="TPM novel" /> The scene where Jira and Skywalker say goodbye appeared in several of the film's print adaptations and tie-ins,<ref name="TPM novel" /><ref name="Journal" /> and was included on the film's DVD, first released on [[October 16]], [[2001]].<ref name="Insider 56">{{InsiderCite|56|Behind the Episode I: The Phantom Menace DVD|Behind the Episode I: ''The Phantom Menace'' DVD}}</ref> Towner's appearance in ''The Phantom Menace'' led to increased recognition for the actress, who attended various ''Star Wars'' conventions across the [[Wikipedia:United Kingdom|United Kingdom]] and posed for photographs with fans at her house in [[Wikipedia:Twickenham|Twickenham]] until her death on [[April 10]], [[2017]]. Her obituary in [[Wikipedia:The Daily Telegraph|''The Daily Telegraph'']] prominently discussed her role in ''The Phantom Menace''.<ref name="Obituary" />

===Other appearances===
{{Quote|An ''Unleashed'' figure of Jira could portray her doing a variety of exciting things&ndash;selling fruit, making change, retelling that old tale of the mysterious wandering "Nobot," or just looking vacantly into the distance for stormclouds.|Bonnie Burton, writing a humurous description of a hypothetical Jira action figure|<ref name="Checklist">{{SWArchive|url=collecting/news/hasbro/f20071205/indexp2.html|text=Checklist: 10 Unlikely Unleashed Figures}}</ref>}}
[[File:Jira action figure.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Pablo Hidalgo's concept art for an action figure of Jira]]
[[Heidi Shannon]] was credited for voicing Jira in the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|adaptation of ''The Phantom Menace'']],<ref name="TPM game">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref> which was released on [[May 18]], 1999.<ref name="IGN">{{WebCite|url=https://www.ign.com/articles/1999/05/18/star-wars-hits-the-shelves|text=Star Wars Hits The Shelves|author=IGN Staff|date=1999-05-18|work=[[Wikipedia:IGN|IGN]]|archivedate=20121121210047}}</ref> However, the character did not appear in the finished game.<ref name="TPM game" /> Jira did appear in the [[Canon|non-canon]] racing game ''[[Star Wars: Super Bombad Racing]]'',<ref name="Super Bombad">''[[Star Wars: Super Bombad Racing]]''</ref> released on [[April 23]], [[2001]],<ref name="Release">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/videogames/news/news20010416.html|text=Super Bombad Racing at the Metreon}}</ref> in which she served as the flag waver for the Mos Espa racetrack.<ref name="Super Bombad" />

In a feature published on [[StarWars.com]] on [[December 5]], [[2007]], Jira was named by author [[Bonnie Burton]] as one of the ten most unlikely ''Star Wars'' characters to receive an [[Star Wars Unleashed|''Unleashed'' series]] action figure. However, the article included a hypothetical figure sketch of the character drawn by [[Pablo Hidalgo]].<ref name="Checklist" />
